claims.claim: In Nguyen and colleagues' human evaluation at temperature 3 with the lower-diversity setting, min-p stories scored 7.74 out of 10 for quality against 5.75 for top-p and 6.75 for standard sampling.

claims.page: Table 4 (row T=3, Quality, Lower Diversity Settings)

claims.claim: Nguyen and colleagues report min-p winning 56.54 percent on the AlpacaEval Creative Writing benchmark at temperature 1.5, against 53.18 percent for temperature-only sampling.
claims.source: Nguyen Nhat Minh, Andrew Baker, Clement Neo, Allen Roush, Andreas Kirsch and Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, 'Turning Up the Heat: Min-p Sampling for Creative and Coherent LLM Outputs', ICLR 2025 (arXiv v8, 20 Nov 2025)
claims.page: Table 3b (AlpacaEval Creative Writing % win, column tau=1.5)

claims.claim: Nguyen and colleagues concede that their human evaluation rests on a limited sample size and gives directional insight rather than a settled result.
claims.source: Nguyen Nhat Minh, Andrew Baker, Clement Neo, Allen Roush, Andreas Kirsch and Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, 'Turning Up the Heat: Min-p Sampling for Creative and Coherent LLM Outputs', ICLR 2025 (arXiv v8, 20 Nov 2025)

claims.claim: Nguyen and colleagues relay, from Ilya Gusev's run of Sam Paech's EQ-Bench Creative Writing benchmark, a min-p score of 62 at temperature 1.5 against the baseline's 51.5 at temperature 1.0.
claims.source: Nguyen Nhat Minh, Andrew Baker, Clement Neo, Allen Roush, Andreas Kirsch and Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, 'Turning Up the Heat: Min-p Sampling for Creative and Coherent LLM Outputs', ICLR 2025 (arXiv v8, 20 Nov 2025)

claims.claim: Basu and colleagues measured that sentence-level repetition in GPT-2 output effectively disappears above an observed cross-entropy of about 2.5.
claims.source: Sourya Basu, Govardana Sachitanandam Ramachandran, Nitish Shirish Keskar and Lav R. Varshney, 'Mirostat: A Neural Text Decoding Algorithm that Directly Controls Perplexity', ICLR 2021 (arXiv v2, 14 Jan 2021)
claims.quote: beyond a threshold of cross-entropy, which seems to be around 2.5

claims.claim: Basu and colleagues measured that human-written continuation settles at a limiting cross-entropy rate as it lengthens, falling into neither the boredom nor the confusion trap.
claims.source: Sourya Basu, Govardana Sachitanandam Ramachandran, Nitish Shirish Keskar and Lav R. Varshney, 'Mirostat: A Neural Text Decoding Algorithm that Directly Controls Perplexity', ICLR 2021 (arXiv v2, 14 Jan 2021)
claims.quote: Human-generated text converges to some limiting value of cross-
claims.page: section 5.3, Boredom and Confusion Traps, discussion of Figure 5c

claims.claim: Basu and colleagues report that at a target cross-entropy of 3 more than half their raters guessed the AI-generated text was human-written.
claims.source: Sourya Basu, Govardana Sachitanandam Ramachandran, Nitish Shirish Keskar and Lav R. Varshney, 'Mirostat: A Neural Text Decoding Algorithm that Directly Controls Perplexity', ICLR 2021 (arXiv v2, 14 Jan 2021)
claims.quote: more than half of raters mistakenly guessed the AI-generated text

claims.claim: Basu and colleagues measured that GPT-2-XL at 1558 million parameters repeats slightly less than GPT-2 at 117 million parameters at the same observed cross-entropy.
claims.source: Sourya Basu, Govardana Sachitanandam Ramachandran, Nitish Shirish Keskar and Lav R. Varshney, 'Mirostat: A Neural Text Decoding Algorithm that Directly Controls Perplexity', ICLR 2021 (arXiv v2, 14 Jan 2021)
claims.quote: have slightly less repetitions for a fixed value of cross-entropy

claims.claim: Su and colleagues measured cosine similarities above 0.95 between the representations of different tokens within a single sentence in GPT-2.
claims.source: Yixuan Su, Tian Lan, Yan Wang, Dani Yogatama, Lingpeng Kong and Nigel Collier, 'A Contrastive Framework for Neural Text Generation', NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv v3, 26 Sep 2022)
claims.quote: the cosine similarities between tokens within a sentence are over 0.95

claims.claim: Su and colleagues ran their whole degeneration evaluation on the Wikitext-103 test set, that is on encyclopedic prose.
claims.source: Yixuan Su, Tian Lan, Yan Wang, Dani Yogatama, Lingpeng Kong and Nigel Collier, 'A Contrastive Framework for Neural Text Generation', NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv v3, 26 Sep 2022)
claims.page: Table 1 caption: 'Evaluation results on Wikitext-103 test set'

claims.claim: In Su and colleagues' Wikitext-103 table, greedy decoding from the MLE model scored a rep-2 of 69.21 against 3.92 for the human reference.
claims.source: Yixuan Su, Tian Lan, Yan Wang, Dani Yogatama, Lingpeng Kong and Nigel Collier, 'A Contrastive Framework for Neural Text Generation', NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv v3, 26 Sep 2022)
claims.page: Table 1 (column rep-2, rows MLE greedy and Human)

claims.claim: In Su and colleagues' Wikitext-103 table, nucleus sampling produced text with a generation perplexity of 47.19 against 24.01 for the human reference, so the sampled text was less predictable than the human original rather than flatter.
claims.source: Yixuan Su, Tian Lan, Yan Wang, Dani Yogatama, Lingpeng Kong and Nigel Collier, 'A Contrastive Framework for Neural Text Generation', NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv v3, 26 Sep 2022)
claims.page: Table 1 (column gen-ppl, rows SimCTG nucleus and Human)

verdicts.trueWording: Table 4, T=3 Quality: Standard 6.75, Top-p 5.75, Min-p 7.74
verdicts.note: arXiv v8 full-text HTML (arxiv.org/html/2407.01082v8) read raw. Table 4, row T=3 / Quality, Lower Diversity Settings: Standard Sampling 6.75+/-0.3509, Top-p=0.1 5.75+/-0.3201, Min-p=0.2 7.74+/-0.2418. Caption confirms the 1-10 scale. Claim carries no quotation, so graded on substance; every figure is exact.

Same raw v8 HTML. Table 3 right panel is headed '(b) AlpacaEval Creative Writing (% win)'; column tau=1.5 gives Temperature Only 53.18 and Min-p (ours) 56.54 (top-p has no tau=1.5 entry). No quotation supplied, so substance.

verdicts.trueWording: this represents a limited sample size, it provides valuable directional insights
verdicts.note: Section 6 Human Evaluation, Experimental Setup paragraph reads 'While this represents a limited sample size, it provides valuable directional insights into perceived quality and diversity differences between methods.' The supplied quote is a contiguous substring (drops the leading 'While'); both limbs (limited sample, directional not settled) are on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: min-p (tau=1.5) scoring 62 versus the baseline's 51.5 at tau=1.0
verdicts.note: Creative Writing results paragraph (sec. 5.2, before 5.3 Ablation Study), raw v8 HTML: 'Independent EQ-Bench Creative Writing Paech (2024) results further support these findings, with min-p (tau=1.5, p_base=0.1) scoring 62 versus the baseline's 51.5 at tau=1.0 (Gusev, 2024).' Reference list confirms Samuel J. Paech (EQ-Bench) and Ilya Gusev. Section label in the claim is 5.2, not 5.2.3, in this version.

verdicts.trueWording: beyond a threshold of cross-entropy, which seems to be around 2.5
verdicts.note: ar5iv full text of 2007.14966 (v2), section 5.2 'Perplexity and repetitions', Fig. 3c paragraph: '...we do expect a good sampling algorithm to have minimum sentence-level repetitions, which all the sampling seems to show beyond a threshold of cross-entropy, which seems to be around 2.5 for GPT-2.' Quote contiguous; sentence-level, GPT-2 and observed cross-entropy limbs all present.

verdicts.trueWording: Human-generated text converges to some limiting value of cross-entropy
verdicts.note: Section 5.3 'Boredom and confusion traps', Fig. 5c paragraph: 'Human-generated text converges to some limiting value of cross-entropy when the generated text is long enough and does not fall into either boredom or confusion.' The supplied quote truncates mid-word at 'cross-' but is contiguous; the neither-trap limb is in the same sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: more than half of raters mistakenly guessed the AI-generated text
verdicts.note: Section 5.4 Human Evaluations: 'Further, for tau=3, more than half of raters mistakenly guessed the AI-generated text to be human generated.' tau is the target average cross-entropy rate set for mirostat, matching the claim's 'target cross-entropy of 3'. 43 participants.

verdicts.trueWording: have slightly less repetitions for a fixed value of cross-entropy
verdicts.note: Section 5.2, Fig. 3d paragraph: 'Larger LMs such as GPT-2-XL with 1558M parameters have slightly less repetitions for a fixed value of cross-entropy than smaller LMs such as GPT-2 with 117M parameters.' Figure 3 caption repeats it. Both parameter counts on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: the cosine similarities between tokens within a sentence are over 0.95
verdicts.note: ar5iv full text of 2202.06417 (v3), section 1 Introduction, Figure 1(a) discussion: 'We see that the cosine similarities between tokens within a sentence are over 0.95, meaning that these representations are close to each other.' The matrix is GPT-2 output-layer token representations.

verdicts.trueWording: Table 1 caption: Evaluation results on Wikitext-103 test set
verdicts.note: Table 1 caption is exactly that; section 4 Evaluation Benchmark describes Wikitext-103 as a large collection of Wikipedia articles, supporting 'encyclopedic prose'. Checked the 'whole' limb adversarially: the only other task, section 5 open-domain dialogue (LCCC, DailyDialog), reports human ratings alone, no rep-n/diversity/MAUVE/gen-ppl, so every degeneration measurement in the paper is on Wikitext-103.
Table 1 (Wikitext-103 test set), rep-2 column: MLE + greedy 69.21; Human row 3.92. Both figures exact; no quotation supplied, so substance.

Table 1 gen-ppl column: SimCTG + nucleus 47.19, Human 24.01 (MLE + nucleus is 49.71, so the row attribution in the claim's page field is the right one). The interpretive limb is on the page too: section 4.1 defines gen-ppl and states a high gen-ppl means the generated text is very unlikely given the prefix, i.e. less predictable, not flatter.

verdicts.trueWording: results in 9,000 annotated samples in total
verdicts.note: Section 4.3 Human Evaluation: 200 prefixes of length 32 randomly selected from the Wikitext-103 test set, all generations plus the reference shuffled and 'evaluated by five graders, which results in 9,000 annotated samples in total'. All three limbs present.

verdicts.trueWording: our reanalysis demonstrates min-p did not outperform baseline samplers
verdicts.note: arXiv v2 full-text HTML (arxiv.org/html/2506.13681v2), Abstract: '...our reanalysis demonstrates min-p did not outperform baseline samplers in quality, diversity, or a trade-off between quality and diversity.' The supplied quote is the contiguous head of that clause. Authors and Stanford affiliation confirmed on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: the three samplers provide similar quality and similar diversity
verdicts.note: Section 2.2 (Visualizations and Statistical Tests Fail to Support...), Figure 1 discussion: 'Using the original paper's data, Fig. 1 reveals that the three samplers provide similar quality and similar diversity, with 95% confidence intervals frequently overlapping.' Both metric limbs and the overlapping-CI limb are in the one sentence.
